AccessDeniedResponse.description:
Access Denied Response (403).

Your account does not have the required permissions to access this resource.

example: The key "username" must be a string.

BadRequestResponse.description:
Bad Request Response (400).

Check your request for malformed or missing parameters.

NotAcceptableResponse.description:
Not Acceptable Response (406).

Check the response content for further error details.

In some cases, a detail error code may be returned:

- `4` - Subscription not found
- `5` - Email address validation failed
- `7` - Subscriber email not found
- `8` - Field validation failed
- `9` - Subscriber not subscribed
- `10` - Subscriber update failed
- `30` - Email address change not allowed
- `31` - Untag smarttag not allowed
- `32` - Email address SMS number required
- `100` - Invalid API key
- `401` - User not found
- `402` - List not found
- `403` - Tag not found
- `404` - User group not found
- `405` - Campaign not found
- `406` - Tier not found
- `501` - Email address required
- `502` - Username required
- `503` - Password required
- `504` - First name required
- `505` - Last name required
- `506` - Username exists
- `507` - Email address exists
- `508` - User update failed

multidimensional.description: Whether a contact can hold one value per subscription (true) or one value overall (false)

name.description: Name of the data field; unique within the account, at most 250 characters, no HTML

type.description: Data field type, one of `field-single`, `field-paragraph`, `field-email`, `field-number`, `field-url`, `field-date`, `field-time`, `field-datetime`, `field-html`, `field-decimal` (the types returned by `GET /field/{fieldid}?detail=true`)

listid.description: Internal ID of the opt-in process

email.description:
Valid email address and must contain `@`.

Either `email` or `smsnumber` is required.
Email address must be unique per contact.

fields.description: Additional custom fields for the subscriber. Keys must match the field names configured in KlickTipp. Each field expects a specific data format depending on its field type. For raw `Time` fields, an empty string, JSON `false`, or JSON `null` clears in either mode. PHP's `http_build_query()` encodes `false` as `0` (clears in `legacy`, stores midnight in `seconds`) and omits `null`. - `Line`: Single-line text without line breaks. Example: `Alex Example` - `Paragraph`: Text with paragraphs. Use `\n` to separate paragraphs. Example: `Dies ist ein Text.\nMit Absatz.` - `Number`: Integer value. No dot, no comma. Example: `42` - `Decimal Number`: Decimal value. Output always uses a dot as decimal separator. Example: Input `1999` → Output `19.99` - `URL`: Valid web address. Must start with `http://` or `https://`. Example: `https://klicktipp.com` - `Time`: Seconds since midnight between `0` and `86399`. `0` clears by default; set top-level `time_value_mode` to `seconds` to store midnight. Raw clock strings such as `00:00` are not accepted. Example: `52200` (14:30 GMT) - `Date`: Unix timestamp in seconds. Date formats like `DD.MM.YYYY` are not supported. Example: `1715126400` (08.05.2024 GMT) - `Date & Time`: Unix timestamp in seconds. Do not send formatted date strings or values with spaces. Example: `1715603400` (13.05.2024 12:30:00 GMT) - `HTML`: HTML-formatted content. Only use this type if the field explicitly allows HTML. Example: `Hello World`

listid.description:

Either `email` or `smsnumber` is required.
SMS number must be unique per contact.

  Accepted input:

  - `004912345678`

  Stored format:
- `004912345678`

tagid.description:

Used for segmentation and automation triggers.

time_value_mode.description:
Controls raw `Time` field values for this request only.

Omit or use `legacy` to preserve zero-clearing: a value that becomes exactly `"0"` after scalar conversion clears the field.
Use `seconds` to store `0` or `"0"` as midnight, including values read from GET responses.
An empty string clears in both modes; other field types are unchanged.
Only the exact strings `legacy` and `seconds` are accepted; supplied null or any other value returns HTTP 406 before writing.
Enable `seconds` in clients only after upgrading the server.

info.description:
This specification describes the **KlickTipp Management API**. It is intended for developers and integrators who want to interact directly with KlickTipp to manage contacts, tags, custom fields, opt-in processes, and automation workflows. The API can be used standalone or through third-party platforms. The specification focuses on correct request formats, authentication mechanisms, response structures, and error handling to ensure reliable and predictable integrations. **Good to know:** This API uses session-based cookie authentication. Interactive Try-It requests do not fully support this login flow. For production testing click on the button to open our Collection in Postman.
--- ## Base URL The base URL for the KlickTipp API production environment is: ``` https://api.klicktipp.com ``` All endpoints defined in this specification are relative to this base URL. --- ## Getting Started To access the API, you must authenticate and maintain a valid session. 1. **Authentication** Most endpoints require cookie-based authentication. Use the login endpoint with your KlickTipp username and password to obtain a **session cookie**, which must be sent with all subsequent requests. 2. **Request Preparation** Replace all placeholder values such as email addresses, IDs, or timestamps with valid test data. Invalid formats are a common source of errors. 3. **Response Handling** The API returns structured payloads and numeric error codes. Always validate HTTP status codes and response bodies programmatically. --- ## Authentication Overview The KlickTipp Management API supports **multiple authentication models**, depending on the integration scenario. - **Username and password authentication via session cookie** Typically used for internal tools and administrative workflows. - **Developer key and customer key authentication** Intended for long-running, production-grade, or multi-tenant integrations. This model does not rely on session handling. Documentation: [How to authenticate and access the Management API](https://developers.klicktipp.com/guides/management-api-authentication) --- ## Response Format The KlickTipp Management API uses JSON as its response format. All endpoints return **JSON responses**, including structured data, timestamps, and error details. Integrations are expected to consume and validate JSON exclusively. --- ## Data Formats and Validation Date and time values must always be provided as **Unix timestamps (seconds)**. Formatted date strings, locale-specific formats, and timezone annotations are **not supported**. Incorrect field formats are a frequent cause of validation errors. Always ensure that submitted values match the expected field type definitions. Documentation: [Data field types and Inputs](https://developers.klicktipp.com/guides/data-field-types) --- ## Error Handling Errors are typically returned with **HTTP status code 406** and include a numeric error code in the response body. Integrations should handle errors explicitly and provide meaningful diagnostics for debugging and monitoring. Documentation: [Error Handling](https://developers.klicktipp.com/guides/error-handling) --- This specification is designed to support stable, predictable, and maintainable integrations with the KlickTipp platform.

get.description:
Lists data fields. Without `detail=true`, each key maps to its name; with `detail=true`, each key maps to an object with `name` and `type`. All entries in a response use the same format.

Collection keys are prefixed with `field` (for example `field12345` or `fieldFirstName`). Remove that prefix when calling `GET /field/{fieldid}`: use `/field/12345` or `/field/FirstName`.

parameters.description: Return the name and type for each data field.
parameters.name: detail

post.description:
Creates a data field with its type, dimensionality and AI description. The field behaves like one created in the app: it appears in the field overview, can be used as a placeholder, filled through the contact endpoints and used in campaigns.

A rejected request creates no field. The response lists one message per problem, naming the attribute and, where applicable, the allowed values or length; a duplicate name names the ID of the existing field.

id.description: ID of the new data field

example: type: Unknown data field type "datetime". Allowed values: field-single, field-paragraph, field-email, field-number, field-url, field-date, field-time, field-datetime, field-html, field-decimal.
name: A data field with this name already exists (id 213736).

406.description: Not Acceptable Response (406). The data field was not created.

get.description:
Gets a data field by its unprefixed ID. For example, collection key `field12345` is retrieved with `/field/12345`; `fieldFirstName` with `/field/FirstName`. Without `detail=true`, the response contains `id` and `name`; `detail=true` also adds `type`, `multidimensional`, `ai_description`, `category`, and `meta_labels`. All detailed properties are always present, including empty strings and an empty label array when no metadata is configured. The type vocabulary is extensible; clients should handle unfamiliar tokens. Current types (JSON value types and input examples for writing contact field values): | Type | Meaning | JSON value / input format | Example | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `field-single` | Single-line text | String | `"Alex"` | | `field-paragraph` | Multiline text | String | `"Line 1\nLine 2"` | | `field-email` | Email address | String containing a valid email address | `"alex@example.com"` | | `field-number` | Whole number | JSON integer | `100` | | `field-url` | URL | String with absolute `http://` or `https://` URL | `"https://example.com"` | | `field-date` | Calendar date | JSON integer, Unix timestamp in seconds | `755222400` | | `field-time` | Time of day | JSON integer, seconds since midnight (0–86399) | `52200` | | `field-datetime` | Date and time | JSON integer, Unix timestamp in seconds representing a UTC instant | `1715603400` | | `field-html` | HTML content | String containing HTML | `"

Hello

"` | | `field-decimal` | Decimal number | JSON integer scaled by 100 (1999 displays as 19.99) | `1999` | | `field-unknown` | Legacy or unsupported field type (e.g. dropdown, checkbox or internal array) | No reliable input format; do not derive validation behavior from this token | — | For date and date-time values use seconds, not milliseconds or formatted date strings. Convert local date-times to a UTC instant before sending.
